body:
**[high]** resolveMember() is now a check-then-create path with no idempotency guard. The app already issues concurrent CDP resolves for the same user, for example the Affiliations view fetches project affiliations and work experiences in the same forkJoin, and the profile layout can fetch identities for tab notifications. For a first-time user, two requests can both resolve no member and both POST /v1/members with the same LFID identity. Depending on CDP behavior, that either creates duplicate CDP members or makes one request fail with a duplicate/conflict and the UI falls back to an empty state, which is the class of silent-empty behavior this PR is trying to fix. Make the create step idempotent before putting it in this shared read chokepoint.

_Suggested fix:_ Use an in-flight promise map keyed by LFID inside CdpService, call an upstream idempotent resolve-or-create contract if CDP provides one, or handle duplicate/conflict responses from createMember() by resolving again and returning the existing member ID.

<!-- agentic:pr-reviewer tid=ca39a5829e76456d sev=high -->

**[should-fix]** CdpResolveResponse still declares memberId as always present, but this PR's new branch depends on a successful resolve response where memberId is missing. @lfx-one/shared is the contract surface both sides import, so leaving the field required hides exactly the edge case this change is adding and lets future call sites compile while assuming resolve can never return an empty result. Reflect the actual resolve contract and keep the create response strict separately.

_Suggested fix:_ Model resolve as something like `memberId?: string | null`, introduce a separate create-member response type if create guarantees an ID, and have createMember() throw a MicroserviceError if CDP returns success without a memberId.

<!-- agentic:pr-reviewer tid=4e9291910160e2e6 sev=should-fix -->

**[should-fix]** The new create path logs the raw LFID at info level here and the raw display name at debug level in createMember(). LFIDs/usernames and display names are identity PII, and the logger only redacts configured token/email-style fields; it does not sanitize these metadata keys. This makes first-access profile reads persist user identity/name data in server logs just because CDP had no member yet. Keep the operational signal without logging the raw user identifiers.

_Suggested fix:_ Omit `lfid` and `display_name` from these log metadata objects, or replace them with a stable non-PII/hash value if correlation is required.

<!-- agentic:pr-reviewer tid=83df18734ac684ff sev=should-fix -->
